posts.author: Jesse - PVGames
posts.body:
A new and much-approved version of the Character Maker is available! Thanks to Martin's talents, you can now whip up sprite sheets, paperdolls, busts, and more quickly and easily! On top of that, there is also a level editor that you can use to build your game maps with PVGames assets!
Software Features include:
The ability to quickly and simply create your characters, easily drawing from a large pool of PVGames resources.
Many export options - customize what animations, what directional facings, etc that you want to export.
Save characters and character templates. An auto-save feature is also present.
Adjust color, hue, saturation, of any individual piece of equipment or character right from within the editor.
Layer control - change which layer an item is on quickly
Multiple views - While building your character, easily swap between numerous bust, paperdoll, face, and animated sprite views to see your character come alive.
Level editor - easily build maps using PVGames resources, complete with auto Z-level sorting and unlimited layer support, toggleable snap-to-grid, and much more!
You can see both of these in action in this little video here:
PM me for details if you're interested in the software.
Thank you!

posts.author: jerseyware
posts.body:
Awesome tool, just downloaded and tested it. There is no error reporting, so if it doesn't load up, check your file paths!
That said, this gives you ALL of the artwork. Every single cut piece of artwork you can find in the base Male# or Female# folder will be output with the complete clothes you setup in the generator - including SV battlers. I can't imagine how much faster we'll be able to create our NPCs.
The color change tools are a neat idea, but applying color uniformly to detailed clothing pieces doesn't work. This portion will need to be a bit more sophisticated to have a real use. There also doesn't appear to be a way to undo color changes without removing and replacing the clothing piece. Hopefully this tool will become all it can be in the future!
The multi views for preview are terrific for seeing small changes, and layer controls make swapping pieces a breeze.
Overall another great release from PV Games!
EDIT: The color change tools actually work out better than I originally assessed. Some pieces can be given total color repaints and come out just fine. This still won't work out so well with the more detailed chest pieces, but for certain shirts and pants, you'll have no trouble getting a nice variance.

It works best for items that you mentioned, certain shirts and pants, but it shines the brightest with hair and facial hair (and cloaks, tabards, and some other items). Overall it is a very useful tool, but mileage might vary a bit depending on the specific item you are re-coloring.

posts.author: Jesse - PVGames
posts.body:
Heya Jcoultas!
To answer your questions (hopefully):
1.) If you layer the clothing on the templates outside of the software and then put that inside the software, you could theoretically layer more stuff on top of the template but depending what you did to the template outside of the software you might have various visual issues (clothing overlapping in strange ways for example). If relying heavily on the software to generate the materials for you, then it might be best to start with making the character in the generator first and then do edits to it afterwards rather than the other way around.
2.) For shorter or taller characters you would have to edit the character outside of the software, the software by default can't really do it (unless you have the Dwarves from the Underdeep, they have character generator parts that work in the software). The templates' size can't be increased or decreased within the software unfortunately (these are 2D images afterall, not 3D so are not subject to the same sort of deformation tools). As for changing character scale in-game, I am sure it can be done with a script or plug-in. I know there was a script for VX Ace that allowed this to some degree, no clue about a plug-in for MV though. You are better off just having the character spritesheets and whatnot edited though, you will have a better and more consistent quality if the editor knows what they are doing

There are no characters in the Diseased town set, that is just a small add-on that gives dirtied versions of tiles from some of the other packs. The Underdeep does contain a bunch of clothing and templates though for the character generator. It has Dwarves, Orcs, and Drow templates and clothing for all three. The Dwarves are a unique shape (shorter and stalkier than the human templates) and their clothing will work only with those templates. The Orcs and Drow templates and clothing will work with all human templates and vice versa.

For the map (character) view you want any of the files that show 3 images of a character across and 4 rows deep. By default, MV uses character sheets that have this format pasted 4 times across with another row of 4 under that so you only need 1 file to store map (character) view sprites for 8 characters. Hence, you need to increase the image size of whichever of the files you decided on that I mentioned before to be 4x the original pixel width and 2x the original pixel height. So just take your desired file into PhotoShop if you have it, GIMP if you don't (GIMP is free to download and similar to PhotoShop), open your desired file, and change the canvas size 4x as wide and 2x as tall and save it out and you should be able to use that in MV. Hope it helps!
EDIT: Please note you are just changing the dimensions of the image itself, not scaling anything. Changing the dimensions will create a large blank space, but MV by default only looks at the horizontal of these images 1/4 at a time and only the top or bottom 1/2 when framing the cursor you use to select which of the 8 characters it thinks you have on the sheet, so...you should be good.

Windows File System has a file path character limit of I believe 255 or 260 characters. This is a part of the OS, not the program, and will exist no matter what software you use. Please don't put anything directly on the C:\
Windows has a limit of entries in any directory, but the root is much smaller than all the rest. If you go over a certain number, windows will become intermittently unstable, and eventually fail to boot entirely.
(It's also no where close to a 'best practices' to clutter the root.)
If you need to shorten paths, put all of those into a folder that's on the root, and it can have a really short name if you want it too.
I know microsoft says the 512 limit on root doesn't exist anymore, but it's still not the most stable thing for your machine if you exceed it. Remember, microsoft has no problem calling certain bugs and glitches "undocumented features", and still has issues from previous OS versions that hang around under the band-aids and wallpapering/whitewashing. It's kind of inevitable as long as they maintain the backwards compatibility.
The worst case of this I ran across that was still more or less running had 666,668 entries on the root. Once we cleared that mess out, which took a while, the machine perked right back up to normal and was stable again as well.
Another case was someone that kept installing things directly to the root. Not a different directory on the root, but the root itself. Of course his computer was unstable, but as the stuff he'd installed there were all mixed up together, there were all kinds of issues with mismatched dlls and uninstalls breaking things, etc.
But hey, at least they weren't storing important files in the trash, or putting the swap file in a ramdrive! (Also real things fools have done.)
As a general note, it's good to clear the temp files (tmp) from the root, as well as old log files and other cruft that tends to build up on many machines.

posts.body: Not sure if this has been mentioned, but if anyone's using Galv's Character Frames, Character Animations and 8-direction Movement plugins, you can create a character sheet really easily using the Custom Sheet function of the Character Creator. You just need to select Idle, Walking and Running animations in all 8 directions and then export the sheet. You still have to lay out the three sets of exported sprites in the Idle, Walking, Running and Blank horizontal sequence that Galv's plug-ins require, but this is very straightforward in something like Gimp, and much faster than copying each frame in a particular sequence as was required before. I think there were a few questions about this earlier on in the posts, so believe that answers those, and should be helpful for anyone using these assets in their games to get smooth, 8-directional movement with running and idle animations (which look way cool!). Many thanks to Martin for making this possible.
